subject: SIG: Breach notification — SLA windows, escalation contacts, evidence handoff
messages:
From: Alex Greene <alex.greene@greenfintech.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: security@greenfintech.com
Date: Sat, 02 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SIG follow-up: breach-notice timelines and contacts

Hi Vivek / Laura,

Thanks for the SIG draft you returned last week. Our info-sec team had two follow-ups specifically on Incident Response / Breach Notification:

1) What is Redwood's SLA for initial customer notification once an incident is confirmed (hours after confirmation)? Do you have different windows for US vs EU customers (GDPR expectations)?
2) Who are the on-call contacts for notification (ops, legal, PR)? We need role + phone and an escalation matrix (primary, secondary, 24x7).
3) What evidence do you provide to customers as part of a breach response (logs, audit trail, packet captures are out of scope — but SOC 2 evidence, IR timeline, remediation steps)? Can you attach an example or point to a template?

If you can reply with a short matrix and an example notice template we can attach to our procurement packet, that would help speed things up.

Appreciate it — small timeline on our end: procurement needs signed SIG + clarifications by May 7.

Best,
Alex
Alex Greene
Head of Security Operations
GreenFinTech

--

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Alex Greene <alex.greene@greenfintech.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 02 May 2026 13:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: breach-notice timelines and contacts

Alex — thanks for the clear asks. Quick answers up front, then attachments and a short escalation matrix below.

1) Initial customer notification: our target is 72 hours from confirmation for incidents that meet breach criteria. For EU customers we follow the same 72-hour target to align with GDPR; in practice we aim for 24–48 hours for high-severity incidents and push legal review in-parallel.

2) On-call escalation (high-level):
- Primary: Incident Response Ops (pager) — incident@redwood.com (24x7)
- Secondary: Security Lead (Vivek Kulkarni) — +1-415-555-0142 (work)
- Legal escalation: Laura Bennett — laura_bennett@redwood.com; +1-650-555-0199
- Communications / PR: Hannah Schmitt — hannah_schmitt@redwood.com

3) Evidence handoff: we provide a tailored evidence bundle that typically includes SOC 2 relevant artifacts, timeline of events, affected resource list, redacted logs where appropriate, and remediation steps. We do not provide raw packet captures or customer PII logs.

Attachments: attached is a draft SIG response (SIG_q_complete_v1.pdf), an internal IR roster export (IR_roster_v3.csv) and a short breach-notice template (breach-notice-template.docx).

Summary escalation matrix (high severity):
- 0–1h: Pager alert to IR Ops team; initial triage started.
- 1–6h: Confirm scope; notify Security Lead and Legal if customer data impacted.
- 6–24h: Draft notification; coordinate with customer and legal.
- 24–72h: Send notification to affected customers once confirmed and reviewed by Legal.

I uploaded the same artifacts to our shared drive (link below). Let me know if you want a one-page version you can attach to procurement.

Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Alex — a couple of clarifications from legal side: when we say '72 hours from confirmation' we mean 72 hours from the time Redwood determines the incident meets definition of a reportable breach (not from initial detection). That determination includes scope and impact assessment. In the EU context we will aim to complete the legal assessment within 24h where feasible to avoid unnecessary delay.

Also: procurement teams sometimes ask whether Redwood will notify customer legal teams directly or via the customer admin contact. Our standard is to notify the designated security contact first and copy the customer legal contact if one is listed in account settings. If you want us to notify legal for GreenFinTech directly, please provide the preferred legal contact.

-Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

Alex

Alex — quick follow to close the loop.

1) Attached: a redacted notice (we removed internal ticket IDs and any customer PII) — see breach-notice-template.docx. You can attach this to procurement.
2) Central incident log: yes, we generate a single incident reference (RDW-YYYYMMDD-####) for each incident and include it in customer notifications so customers can correlate with their internal tickets. The incident record is kept in our secure incident system. Retention: incident metadata and timelines are retained for 7 years; detailed telemetry is retained per customer data retention settings and SOC 2 policy (typically 90–365 days depending on artifact type).

- IR Ops (pager): incident@redwood.com (24x7)
